migration_summary: Online concurrent btree index build on a hot table so reads and writes continue while the index is constructed; must run outside an explicit transaction block.
migration_sql: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY by_root_workflow_id ON executions_visibility (namespace_id, root_workflow_id, (COALESCE(close_time, '9999-12-31 23:59:59')) DESC, start_time DESC, run_id);
schema_summary: Same executions_visibility hot path as Temporal issue 6273; pattern recommended as the fix.

risk_flags.message: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY fails if the migration runner wraps it in BEGIN/COMMIT.

risk_narrative: Concurrent index builds avoid long write locks but require multiple internal transaction boundaries. Migration tools that always wrap DDL in a transaction will reject CONCURRENTLY at runtime. Failed builds can leave INVALID indexes that must be dropped outside a transaction too.
lessons_learned: Use CONCURRENTLY for additive indexes on busy tables; disable transaction wrapping for that statement; set lock_timeout; clean up INVALID indexes if the build fails. Still expect a long wall-clock build on large tables even when online.
surprise_notes: The safer online form is rejected by default migration runners unless you opt out of the surrounding transaction—silent footgun when copying the Temporal suggested fix.

prediction_summary.risk_explanation: Online build is safer for writers but slower wall-clock than blocking CREATE INDEX.

dimension_details.note: Representative safe pattern from Temporal #6273 discussion; not a separate measured run.
